"NEW IMPROVEMENT — Random Starting Player for Every Round

I noticed an issue with the starting-player selection during consecutive rounds.

For example:

- 10 players start a match.
- Round 1 selects Abdullah as the starting player.
- Voting happens.
- Round 2 begins.
- Abdullah is still selected as the starting player.
- The same thing can continue in later rounds.

I want to change this behaviour.

Required behaviour

Randomly select a starting player at the beginning of EVERY new round.

Requirements:

1. At the beginning of Round 1, randomly select one eligible player.
2. After voting is completed and the next round begins, randomly select a starting player again.
3. The new starting player must be selected from the players who are still active in the match.
4. Do not automatically reuse the previous round's starting player when other eligible players are available.
5. The starting player must be able to change in every round.
6. Eliminated players must never be selected.
7. Every active player should have a fair opportunity to start a round over the course of the match.
8. Do not simply follow the player-list order. Use random selection.

Avoid consecutive repetition

- Exclude the previous round's starting player from the selection pool whenever at least one other eligible player exists.
- Randomly select from the remaining eligible players.
- If only one eligible player remains, allow that player to start.
- Reset the round-level starting-player tracking when a completely new match begins.

Important distinction

There are two separate behaviours:

Between matches:
Keep the existing party-based starting-player rotation system. Avoid selecting the same person who started the previous match whenever possible.

Between rounds within a match:
Randomly select a new starting player from the currently active players after each completed voting phase.

Both systems must work independently without overwriting each other's history.

Preserve existing functionality

- Apply this only to the verbal clue mode when typed clue mode is OFF.
- Keep the existing starting-player display and button behaviour.
- Do not change the role-reveal order.
- Do not change Imposter assignment.
- Do not change voting mechanics, elimination, or win conditions.
- Do not change the existing party system, match history, statistics, or UI theme.

Testing

Verify the following:

- Round 1 selects a random starting player.
- Round 2 selects a new random starting player.
- Round 3 selects again from the remaining active players.
- An eliminated player is never selected.
- The previous round's starter is avoided whenever other eligible players exist.
- The same player can start again if they are the only eligible option.
- Starting-player rotation between separate matches still works.
- Typed clue mode remains unchanged.

Make only these changes. Do not refactor unrelated game systems.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Requirements
- Select only active players; exclude the previous round’s starter whenever another eligible player exists.

- Track the previous round’s starter in in-memory state, reset when starting a new match.

- Validate the edited code and run the requested behavior checks.
- Review whether the existing party-history function’s within-match behavior conflicts with the intended separation.

- (none)

1. Inspect the changes in `app.js`, including the `startGame()`, role-reveal, and `renderRoundResult()` paths.
2. Run syntax checks and practical or targeted tests for all requested scenarios.
3. Fix any issues, then summarize verification; changes are currently uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state and starting-player selection flow.

## Important Context
- Repository already contains the playable game; no rebuild was needed.
- The edit adding the helper was performed by inserting before `renderStartingPlayer()`.
- A targeted edit initially failed because whitespace did not match; the subsequent insertion succeeded.

IMPOSTER — Add Delete Party Functionality

I want to fix one specific issue in the existing party management system.


Currently, when I create multiple parties using the "New Party" button, there is no way to delete a party afterward.


I want to add the ability to delete a party.


1. Add a Delete Party option


- Add a clear Delete Party option for each existing party.
- Make it easy to identify which party will be deleted.
- The delete option should be accessible from the party selection or party management area.
- Do not add unnecessary buttons or clutter the existing interface.
- Match the existing Premium Editorial theme and styling.


2. Add deletion confirmation


Before deleting a party:


- Display a confirmation message.
- Clearly show the name of the party being deleted.
- Provide two options: "Cancel" and "Delete".
- Cancel must close the confirmation without changing anything.
- Delete should permanently remove the selected party.


3. Correct data handling


When a party is deleted:


- Remove that party from the party list.
- Remove its associated player list, party-specific history, scores, statistics, and starting-player rotation data.
- Do not affect any other parties or their saved data.
- If the deleted party is currently active, safely switch to another existing party.
- If no parties remain, show the existing new-party creation flow.
- Prevent the application from referencing a deleted party after deletion.


4. Important restrictions


Only implement party deletion.


- Do not change how parties are created.
- Do not change party switching.
- Do not change player setup.
- Do not change Imposter selection.
- Do not change role reveal or starting-player rotation.
- Do not change voting or game mechanics.
- Do not change match history or statistics for parties that are not deleted.
- Do not redesign any screen.
- Preserve the existing UI theme, layout, and functionality.


5. Testing


Verify that:


- A party can be deleted successfully.
- Cancel leaves the party untouched.
- Deleting one party does not affect other parties.
- Deleting the active party switches safely to another party.
- Deleting the last remaining party allows a new party to be created.
- No deleted party or its data reappears after restarting the application.


Final instruction: Inspect the existing party management implementation, add the smallest possible change, and leave everything else exactly as it is.

IMPOSTER — Mobile UI Layout Correction & Responsive Spacing

I have attached two screenshots showing the current application on a mobile phone.


Please inspect the screenshots and the existing UI implementation carefully.


There are some layout and spacing issues that make the application feel less balanced than it should.


I want you to correct these issues while preserving the existing design.


1. Home screen and party management


In the home screen screenshot:


- The party management card has excessive vertical spacing.
- The Party Stats and Delete Party actions feel too far apart.
- The card should use its available space more efficiently.
- Keep the party selector, New Party button, Party Stats, and Delete Party easy to identify and access.
- Maintain consistent spacing between these elements.
- Avoid unnecessary empty space inside the card.


2. Player setup section


Review the "Who's Playing?" section.


- Make player rows consistently spaced.
- Keep the player names, edit buttons, and remove buttons properly aligned.
- Ensure the Add Player input and button fit comfortably on smaller screens.
- Allow long player lists to scroll naturally.
- Avoid clipping, overlapping, or horizontal overflow.
- Keep the player count indicator properly aligned with the heading.


Do not introduce a player limit.


3. Clue screen layout


In the second screenshot, the clue card occupies only the upper portion of the screen, leaving a very large unused area underneath.


Improve the vertical balance.


- Review the positioning of the round indicator and clue card.
- Keep the clue card comfortably positioned below the header.
- Adjust unnecessary vertical gaps.
- Keep the player-turn information, clue input, and Give Clue button properly aligned.
- Make the screen feel balanced without unnecessarily stretching the card.
- Keep the footer positioned consistently without overlapping the main content.


Do not enlarge components just to fill empty space.


4. Responsive layout across the application


Review all existing screens:


- Home
- Party management
- Player setup
- Game settings
- Role reveal
- Clue and discussion
- Voting
- Final guess
- Results
- Match history
- Statistics


Make sure:


- Layouts adapt to different mobile screen heights and widths.
- Content is not cut off.
- Cards do not have unnecessary fixed heights.
- Scrolling works naturally when content exceeds the available screen space.
- Buttons remain accessible.
- The keyboard does not cover important input fields or action buttons.
- The header and footer do not overlap the main content.
- Spacing remains consistent between screens.


Prefer responsive sizing and content-based heights instead of hardcoded dimensions that only work on one screen size.


5. Preserve the existing design


This is extremely important.


Keep the existing Premium Editorial theme exactly as the visual foundation:


- Warm cream background.
- Dark forest-green elements.
- Lime-green accents.
- Existing gradients.
- Subtle paper texture.
- Existing fonts and typography.
- Rounded cards and buttons.
- Current overall visual identity.


Do not introduce a different theme or colour palette.


Do not redesign the application.


6. Strict restrictions


- Do not change game mechanics.
- Do not change player limits or Imposter selection logic.
- Do not change role-reveal order.
- Do not change starting-player rotation.
- Do not change voting or elimination.
- Do not change party creation or deletion.
- Do not change saved data, history, or statistics.
- Do not remove or rename existing features.
- Do not rewrite unrelated components.


7. Final verification


Test the application on different mobile screen sizes and verify:


- The home screen looks balanced.
- Party management does not contain excessive empty spacing.
- Long player lists remain usable.
- The clue screen does not feel unnecessarily empty or stretched.
- No elements overlap or become inaccessible.
- Scrolling and keyboard behaviour work correctly.
- All existing functionality remains unchanged.


Final instruction: Treat this as a responsive layout correction and visual polish task, not a redesign. Make the smallest necessary changes and preserve everything that is already working.

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s responsive mobile layout while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.
- Retain the safe party-deletion flow.

## Requirements
- Keep party selection, New Party, Party Stats, and Delete Party accessible with tighter spacing.
- Align player rows, fit the add-player form on small screens, and support long lists without clipping or a player limit.
- Balance the clue screen vertically without stretching cards; keep controls accessible and the footer clear of content.
- Review mobile widths/heights, scrolling, keyboard visibility, and varied dimensions.
- Do not change game mechanics, party creation/deletion, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Reuse the existing new-party flow when no parties remain.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented party deletion confirmation, party-specific rotation cleanup, active-party fallback, and empty-party creation flow.
- Added responsive party-action styling and mobile layout overrides for party spacing, player rows/list scrolling, add-player sizing, and clue-feed behavior while the input is focused.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Validate responsive behavior and confirm game and party-deletion behavior remain intact.

### Blocked
- Browser testing is incomplete: a Playwright run started at mobile widths but errored while measuring a missing element (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')`), before producing layout results.

## Next Move
1. Fix the browser test’s assumptions about app content being replaced during game phases, then check representative mobile widths/heights, long player lists, scrolling, keyboard visibility, and footer/content overlap.
2. Confirm party creation/deletion and game behavior remain intact.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout overrides and party-action styling.
- `app.js`: Party deletion flow, empty-party state, and setup markup.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- A previous validation completed successfully: `node --check app.js && git diff --check && git diff --stat && git status --short`.
- A local HTTP server was already using port `8765`; attempting to start another server there failed with `[Errno 98] Address already in use`.

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s responsive mobile layout while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.
- Retain the safe party-deletion flow.

## Requirements
- Keep party selection, New Party, Party Stats, and Delete Party accessible with tighter spacing.
- Align player rows, fit the add-player form on small screens, and support long lists without clipping or a player limit.
- Balance the clue screen vertically without stretching cards; keep controls accessible and the footer clear of content.
- Review mobile widths/heights, scrolling, keyboard visibility, and varied dimensions.
- Do not change game mechanics, party creation/deletion, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Reuse the existing new-party flow when no parties remain.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented party deletion confirmation, party-specific rotation cleanup, active-party fallback, and the empty-party creation flow.
- Added responsive party-action styling and mobile layout overrides for party spacing, player rows/list scrolling, add-player sizing, and clue-feed behavior while the input is focused.
- Browser-tested responsive setup at 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 430×740, and 667×375; confirmed no horizontal overflow, long-list scrolling, aligned row controls, and player addition beyond 36 players.
- Browser-tested role reveal/handoff and a complete three-player clue round through to discussion.
- Browser-tested deletion confirmation/cancel, party fallback, rotation cleanup, empty-party state, and creating a new party afterward.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Party deletion flow, empty-party state, setup markup, and game behavior.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout overrides and party-action styling.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Browser checks passed; the app server used was `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

IMPOSTER — FIX THE ACTUAL MOBILE LAYOUT AND ELEMENT PLACEMENT

I previously requested UI spacing improvements, but the resulting screenshots show that the layout has barely changed.

This time, I want you to investigate the actual layout structure and correct the placement of the elements.

Do not just adjust random margins or padding. Identify the components responsible for the excessive spacing and fix their layout rules.

Use my attached screenshots as the reference for the current problems.

1. HOME SCREEN — Correct the vertical arrangement

The home screen should follow this exact visual hierarchy:

1. Application header.
2. Hero section containing:
   - "A PARTY GAME FOR 3+ PLAYERS"
   - "One word. One liar."
   - Short description on the right.
3. Party Management card.
4. Who's Playing card.
5. Remaining game settings and Start Game button, in their existing order.

Party Management card

The current card is unnecessarily tall.

Arrange its contents as follows:

- "PLAYING AS A PARTY" label at the top.
- Party selector directly underneath.
- New Party button directly underneath the selector.
- Party Stats action underneath the New Party button.
- Delete Party action underneath Party Stats.

Spacing instructions:

- Use approximately 12–16px between closely related elements.
- Use approximately 16–20px between action groups.
- Remove excessive vertical gaps.
- Reduce unnecessary bottom padding.
- Keep all actions inside the existing card.

Do not make the card wider or introduce a new design.

2. WHO'S PLAYING — Correct the card layout

The player setup card should follow this structure:

Top row

- "Who's playing?" aligned to the left.
- Player count indicator aligned to the right.

Input row

- Name input on the left.
- Add Player button on the right.
- Both controls should have matching heights and remain usable on smaller screens.

Player list

- Player rows immediately below the input.
- Consistent row heights and spacing.
- Player avatar, name, edit icon and remove icon properly aligned.
- No overlapping or clipping.

Bottom row

- "Add as many players as you like." on the left.
- "Randomize order" on the right.

Keep this bottom row inside the player card, with reasonable spacing above it.

Do not allow the player list to push these controls outside the card.

For large player lists, let the page scroll naturally. Do not impose a player limit or hide players.

3. CLUE SCREEN — Fix the card's internal spacing and position

This is particularly important.

In my screenshot, the clue card starts near the top, but it contains excessive empty space below the Give Clue button.

Use this exact structure:

Header

- Existing application header.

Round information

- "ROUND 1 · CLUE ROUND" aligned left.
- Round counter aligned right.

Clue card

- Heading: "One clue. Keep it clever."
- Existing "NO SAYING THE WORD" label.
- Player turn information card.
- One-word clue input.
- Give Clue button.

Below the clue card

- Existing hint text: "HINTS, NOT DEFINITIONS. GIVE THEM SOMETHING TO DISCUSS."

Clue card spacing

- Keep approximately 24–32px between the round information and the clue card.
- Keep approximately 20–24px internal card padding.
- Use approximately 16–20px between the heading and player information.
- Use approximately 20px between player information and clue input.
- Keep the Give Clue button immediately below the input, with approximately 12px spacing.
- Remove the excessive blank area underneath the button.
- The card height should be determined by its actual content and padding, not an unnecessarily large fixed height.
- Place the hint text approximately 16–20px below the card.

Do not stretch the clue card to fill the screen.

4. FIX THE OVERALL SCREEN LAYOUT

Investigate the application's main page container and screen-specific containers.

Use a proper responsive layout structure.

Expected behaviour:

- The application should respect the available mobile viewport.
- The header should remain at the top of the application layout.
- Main content should flow naturally from top to bottom.
- The footer should sit at the bottom when the page content is short.
- When content becomes longer than the available screen, the main page should scroll naturally and the footer should appear after the content.
- Do not position the footer using absolute positioning that causes it to overlap content.
- Do not use large fixed heights to force cards into position.
- Account for Android status-bar and navigation-bar safe areas.
- Use responsive viewport sizing, including "100dvh" where appropriate.
- Avoid horizontal scrolling.
- Avoid content being hidden behind the keyboard.

Important layout principle

Use a consistent page structure:

Header → Main content → Footer

The main content should use a natural vertical flow.

For short screens, reduce unnecessary spacing rather than shrinking text or buttons.

For longer screens, preserve comfortable spacing and allow scrolling.

5. RESPONSIVE TESTING

Test these layouts at minimum:

- 360 × 640
- 360 × 800
- 393 × 852
- 412 × 915

Check:

- Home screen.
- Party Management card.
- Who's Playing card.
- Clue screen.
- Voting screen.
- Results screen.

Do not optimise exclusively for the dimensions of my screenshots.

6. PRESERVE THE EXISTING DESIGN

Keep the existing Premium Editorial visual identity:

- Warm cream background.
- Dark forest-green buttons and elements.
- Lime-green accents.
- Existing gradients and paper texture.
- Existing typography.
- Existing rounded cards.
- Existing icons and visual language.

Do not introduce a new theme or redesign the application.

7. STRICT FUNCTIONALITY RESTRICTIONS

This is a layout-only task.

Do not change:

- Player management logic.
- Party creation or deletion.
- Imposter selection.
- Dynamic Imposter recommendations.
- Role-reveal sequence.
- Starting-player rotation between matches.
- Random starting player between rounds.
- Typed or verbal clue mechanics.
- Voting and elimination.
- Win conditions.
- Final guessing.
- Match history.
- Scoring and statistics.
- Saved party data.

All existing buttons and controls must continue working exactly as before.

8. IMPLEMENTATION AND VERIFICATION

Before making changes:

1. Inspect the actual page and component hierarchy.
2. Identify fixed heights, excessive padding, margins, flex spacing, grid rules and positioning responsible for the current layout.
3. Identify why the previous layout adjustments did not visibly change the screenshots.
4. Make targeted changes to the responsible components and styles.

After implementation:

1. Run the application's build or available validation checks.
2. Inspect the updated layouts at the requested screen sizes.
3. Compare the results against the attached screenshots.
4. Confirm that the excessive empty spaces have actually been corrected.
5. Confirm that no functionality has been broken.

Do not simply report that the UI is fixed. Verify the actual rendered result.

If a layout issue cannot be verified, clearly identify it.

FINAL REQUIREMENT: I want an actual visible improvement in element placement. Do not return with only minor margin adjustments that leave the screenshots looking practically identical. Preserve the existing design and functionality while correcting the layout structure itself.

- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout by fixing the actual page and component structure, with visible improvement and verified rendered results.
- Preserve the existing Premium Editorial design and all game behavior.

- Home hierarchy: header, hero, Party Management card, Who’s Playing card, then existing settings and Start Game; compact Party Management actions inside its card.
- Who’s Playing card: aligned heading/count, usable input and Add Player controls, aligned player rows, and bottom helper/randomize row kept inside the card; long lists must remain accessible and scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Clue screen: retain the specified round information/card/hint order; size the card to its content, remove blank space below Give Clue, and avoid fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow; footer follows short or long content without overlap; account for mobile safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results layouts at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Layout-only scope: do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

- Existing empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve previously implemented party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.

- Earlier responsive work added party-action styling, mobile overrides, long-player-list scrolling, and clue-feed behavior while input is focused.
- Earlier browser checks covered 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 430×740, and 667×375; tested long lists, role reveal, a clue round, and party deletion/fallback/creation flows.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
STATIC_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR"
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?OPENCODE_WEB_DIR must point to worker metadata storage}"
: "${RUNTIME_DIR:?RUNTIME_DIR must point to the worker runtime}"
PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export PORT

cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
/usr/bin/time -p test -f "$STATIC_DIR/index.html"

# This project is plain HTML/CSS/JS with no package manifest or build step.
/usr/bin/time -p mkdir -p "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"
/usr/bin/time -p env PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR" STATIC_DIR="$STATIC_DIR" node -e 'const fs=require("node:fs"); const path=require("node:path"); fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR,"deployment-output.json"), JSON.stringify({project:process.env.PROJECT_DIR,directory:process.env.STATIC_DIR}))'

# Keep the worker's static server in the foreground for controller lifecycle management.
exec /usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
: "${RUNTIME_DIR:?RUNTIME_DIR must point to the worker runtime}"
: "${CAPTURE_URL:?Set CAPTURE_URL to the exact preview URL}"
: "${CAPTURE_DIR:?Set CAPTURE_DIR to an absolute output directory}"

if [[ "$CAPTURE_DIR" != /* ]]; then
  echo 'CAPTURE_DIR must be an absolute path.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

/usr/bin/time -p test -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs"
/usr/bin/time -p test -f "$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json"
/usr/bin/time -p test -f "$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/display"
/usr/bin/time -p mkdir -p "$CAPTURE_DIR"
CAPTURE_DIR="$(/usr/bin/time -p realpath -m "$CAPTURE_DIR")"
case "$CAPTURE_DIR/" in
  "$PROJECT_DIR/"*)
    echo 'CAPTURE_DIR must be outside the project source tree.' >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# The runtime capture implementation owns and closes its Chromium instance,

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing heading/count, player rows, input, Add Player controls, and helper/randomize row usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, remove blank space below Give Clue, and avoid fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions and delete confirmation styling/markup; empty-party state offers new-party creation.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Earlier browser checks covered 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 430×740, and 667×375, including long lists, role reveal, a clue round, and party deletion/fallback/creation flows.
- `git diff --check` passed during this turn.

### Active
- Review responsive flow, ordering, and sizing; make targeted layout-only corrections if needed.
- Verify home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect responsive layout and setup/game markup for requested flow, ordering, and sizing.
2. Make layout-only corrections in `styles.css`, `app.js`, and, if needed, `index.html`, preserving game and party behavior.
3. Verify the requested screens at all four viewport sizes and run available validation.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Main, mobile, game-screen, and responsive layout rules.
- `app.js`: Setup/game rendering and party behavior; has uncommitted changes.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` are modified and uncommitted; latest status showed only those files changed.
- `renderSetup()` orders hero, party bar, then setup grid; the grid places players before settings on mobile.
- `renderClues()` renders turn and entry before clue feed.
- `playwright-cli`, Chromium, and ChromeDriver are available; no browser verification was performed in the latest turn.

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing heading/count, player rows, input, Add Player controls, and helper/randomize row usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, remove blank space below Give Clue, and avoid fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions, delete-confirmation styling/markup, and an empty-party option to create a party.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Earlier browser checks covered 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 430×740, and 667×375, including long lists, role reveal, a clue round, and party deletion/fallback/creation flows.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Review responsive flow, ordering, and sizing; make targeted layout-only corrections if needed.
- Verify home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at all four requested viewport sizes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect responsive CSS and setup/game markup for the requested flow, ordering, and sizing.
2. Make layout-only corrections in `styles.css`, `app.js`, and, if needed, `index.html`, preserving game and party behavior.
3. Verify the requested screens at all four viewport sizes and run available validation.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Main, mobile, game-screen, and responsive layout rules.
- `app.js`: Setup/game rendering and party behavior.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; latest status showed only those files changed.
- `renderSetup()` orders hero, party bar, then setup grid; the grid places players before settings on mobile.
- `renderClues()` renders turn and entry before the clue feed.
- Browser verification was not performed in the latest turn.

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing heading/count, player rows, input, Add Player controls, and helper/randomize row usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, remove blank space below Give Clue, and avoid fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions, delete-confirmation styling/markup, and an empty-party option to create a party.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Earlier browser checks covered 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 430×740, and 667×375, including long lists, role reveal, a clue round, and party deletion/fallback/creation flows.
- Validated with `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.
- Browser-tested the home screen at all four requested viewport sizes; it flows vertically without overlap, with settings and footer naturally below the fold.

### Active
- Verify Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at all four requested sizes, including header/main/footer flow, horizontal overflow, and clue-card sizing.
- Make targeted layout-only corrections if verification identifies issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915 for Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results.
2. Fix any confirmed layout issues without changing game or party behavior.
3. Rerun requested checks and available validation.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout, home, and game-screen styling.
- `app.js`: Setup/game rendering and party behavior.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; latest `git status --short` showed both modified.

- Home measurements showed vertical scrolling and no header/main/footer overlap; other requested screens remain unverified.

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing heading/count, player rows, input, Add Player controls, and helper/randomize row usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, remove blank space below Give Clue, and avoid fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions, delete-confirmation styling/markup, and an empty-party option to create a party.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Earlier browser checks covered 320×568, 375×667, 390×844, 430×740, and 667×375, including long lists, role reveal, a clue round, and party deletion/fallback/creation flows.
- Validated with `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.
- Browser-tested home at all four requested viewport sizes; vertical flow has no overlap, with settings and footer naturally below the fold.
- Measured Party Stats at all four sizes; no horizontal overflow, header/main/footer flow is contiguous, and stats content scrolls as needed.
- Measured Who’s Playing with 18 players at all four sizes; player list scrolls internally and has no horizontal overflow.
- Browser measurements for clue, voting, round results, and game results at all four requested sizes show no horizontal overflow; header/main/footer remain in document flow.
- Clue card is content-sized (371px in the tested setup) and does not stretch to fill the viewport.

### Active
- Review game-screen results for remaining layout defects, especially long result screens and the voting card’s viewport fit; apply targeted layout-only fixes if needed.
- Retest all requested states and viewports after any changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the measured voting and results layouts for any confirmed usability issues at the four target sizes.
2. Make only necessary layout fixes, preserving game behavior and party data.
3. Rerun browser checks and `git diff --check` / `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout, home, and game-screen styling.
- `app.js`: Setup/game rendering and party behavior.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Browser verification uses `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`; it returned HTTP 200.
- Latest browser script directly populated game state for clue, vote, round-result, and game-result phases. At 360×640, the vote card measured 759px tall and the game-result card 982px, so these screens naturally extend below the fold.
- A prior `playwright-cli run-code` attempt failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'const'`; the corrected invocation succeeded.

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing controls usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, and avoid blank space below Give Clue or fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions, delete-confirmation styling/markup, and an empty-party option to create a party.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Earlier browser checks covered smaller viewports, long lists, role reveal, a clue round, and party deletion/fallback/creation flows.
- Validated with `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js` before the latest CSS edit.
- Browser-tested home, Party Stats, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and result layouts at the requested sizes; no confirmed horizontal overflow in those checks, and clue cards remain content-sized.
- Results naturally extend below the fold; measured vote and game-result cards are long at 360×640.

### Active
- Verify the latest `styles.css` change that attempts to keep voting choices in two columns on narrow screens; recent browser measurements still reported a single-column grid.
- Review whether the long voting card creates a usability defect and apply only confirmed layout fixes.
- Rerun requested viewport checks and validation after any changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the active CSS cascade for `.vote-select` at widths ≤430px and reconcile the latest edit with the browser’s measured single-column result.
2. Make targeted layout-only changes if needed, then retest all requested states and viewports.
3. Run `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and latest voting-grid adjustment.
- `app.js`: Game-screen rendering and party behavior.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; the latest edit modified only `styles.css`.
- Browser testing uses `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`; it returned HTTP 200.
- Recent measurements for vote, round result, and game result showed no horizontal overflow; at 360×640, vote card height was about 759px and game-result card about 982px, with CTAs naturally below the fold.
- After the latest CSS edit, browser measurements at all four target widths still showed a one-column `.vote-select` (one 283–329px grid track), so the attempted two-column adjustment is not yet verified.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing controls usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, and avoid blank space below Give Clue or fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.
- Keep voting choices in two columns on narrow screens; retain results in one column at widths ≤430px.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions, delete-confirmation styling/markup, and an empty-party option to create a party.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Updated mobile vote-choice grid to two columns; browser checks confirmed the two-column layout at 360px.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js` passed after the voting-grid change.

### Active
- Retest home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at all four requested sizes.
- Review long voting-card usability and CTA placement; browser check at 360×640 found the CTA extends below the viewport, while natural document scrolling keeps it reachable.
- Check responsive dimensions and horizontal overflow after the latest CSS changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser retesting the requested states at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915, checking horizontal overflow and control usability.
2. Review vote/result card dimensions and CTA placement; make layout-only changes for confirmed issues.
3. Rerun `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and mobile voting-grid rules.
- `app.js`: Game-screen rendering and party behavior.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Browser tests use `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`; reload or cache-bust `styles.css` when checking changes.
- At 360×800, the vote card is about 573px tall and its CTA fits in the viewport; at 360×640 the document grows vertically and the CTA remains reachable by scrolling.
- Latest browser check at 360px found no horizontal document overflow; the vote card’s internal `scrollWidth` measurement was inconsistent with its visible children, which all fit within the card.

  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url

## Objective
- Correct IMPOSTER’s mobile layout with visible, verified improvements while preserving its Premium Editorial design and game behavior.

## Requirements
- Home order: header, hero, Party Management, Who’s Playing, then settings and Start Game; keep Party Management actions compact within its card.
- Keep Who’s Playing controls usable and aligned; long lists should scroll naturally without a player limit.
- Preserve clue-screen content order, size the card to its content, and avoid blank space below Give Clue or fixed-height stretching.
- Use natural Header → Main → Footer flow without overlap; account for safe areas, dynamic viewport sizing, keyboards, and horizontal overflow.
- Test home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915.
- Keep scope to layout; do not change game mechanics, party management, saved data, or existing features.

## Decisions
- Empty-party flow reuses the new-party creation flow.
- Preserve existing party-deletion confirmation and fallback behavior.
- Keep voting choices in two columns on narrow screens; retain results in one column at widths ≤430px.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added compact Party Management actions, delete-confirmation styling/markup, and an empty-party option to create a party.
- Added mobile player-list scrolling and clue-feed/keyboard layout adjustments.
- Updated mobile vote-choice grid to two columns; browser checks confirmed two columns at 360px.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js` passed after the voting-grid change.
- Browser checks at 360px confirmed no document horizontal overflow; voting CTA remains reachable by vertical scrolling at 360×640 and fits at 360×800.

### Active
- Retest home, Party Management, Who’s Playing, clue, voting, and results at all four requested sizes.
- Investigate vote/result phase-card `scrollWidth` exceeding `clientWidth` at 360px (396px vs 321px); visible children fit within card bounds, and document has no horizontal overflow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser retesting the requested states at 360×640, 360×800, 393×852, and 412×915, checking horizontal overflow and control usability.
2. Review vote/result card dimensions and CTA placement; make layout-only changes for confirmed issues.
3. Rerun `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and mobile voting-grid rules.
- `app.js`: Game-screen rendering and party behavior.
- `index.html`: Header, `main#app`, and footer shell.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Browser checks use `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`.
- At 360×640, the vote card is about 573px tall and its CTA extends below the viewport; natural document scrolling keeps it reachable.
- At 360×800, the vote CTA fits; at 412×915, the vote card is about 539px tall and the CTA fits.
- A 360px viewport reported document width 345px with no horizontal overflow; vote card `scrollWidth` was 396px versus 321px client width, but visible children fit within the card.
